People gather at cafes and outdoor screenings to support team after Spain’s backing for Palestinian rights The Spanish football team’s World Cup win has been celebrated in the streets of Gaza, where Spain’s support for Palestinian rights and Israel’s backing for the Argentinian team turned the competition into more than a football showdown. Gathered at cafes and outdoor screenings, Palestinians defied the risk of Israeli attacks to cheer on a team they had taken to their hearts. Many waving Spanish flags paid tribute to teenage star Lamine Yamal, who brought a Palestinian flag to celebrations for Barcelona’s La Liga win in May. “Whoever raises the Palestinian flag deserves to raise the World Cup,” the Gaza al-Irada amputee football team wrote in a pre-game video message for the Spanish team.

Key takeaways-Gazans gathered in makeshift cafes to watch Spain defeat Argentina 1-0 in the World Cup final, celebrating both the victory and Spain’s support for Palestine. -Residents described the celebrations as an expression of gratitude toward a country widely seen as standing with Palestinians during Israel’s genocide in Gaza. -The final capped months of symbolic gestures linking Spanish football and Palestinian solidarity, from Gaza’s amputee football team to supporters and players in Spain. More than footballFor a few hours on Sunday night, the sounds of war gave way to football. Across the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza, small crowds gathered inside makeshift cafes, their attention fixed on flickering television screens broadcasting the FIFA World Cup final from MetLife Stadium in the United States.

When Spain’s Ferran Torres broke the deadlock in the 105th minute, beating Argentine goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez to secure a 1-0 victory after extra time, celebrations erupted. For many in Gaza, however, the celebrations extended far beyond the football pitch. People who gathered to watch the match said they supported Spain not only because of its football but because the country has increasingly come to symbolize solidarity with the Palestinian people during Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza. Football offers a brief escapeThe World Cup final provided a rare moment of relief for Palestinians living under relentless bombardment, displacement and humanitarian hardship. For several hours, football replaced the daily realities of survival, allowing families and friends to come together despite the difficult conditions.

People gather at cafes and outdoor screenings to support team after Spain’s backing for Palestinian rights

The Spanish football team’s World Cup win has been celebrated in the streets of Gaza, where Spain’s support for Palestinian rights and Israel’s backing for the Argentinian team turned the competition into more than a football showdown.

Gathered at cafes and outdoor screenings, Palestinians defied the risk of Israeli attacks to cheer on a team they had taken to their hearts.

Many waving Spanish flags paid tribute to teenage star Lamine Yamal, who brought a Palestinian flag to celebrations for Barcelona’s La Liga win in May.

“Whoever raises the Palestinian flag deserves to raise the World Cup,” the Gaza al-Irada amputee football team wrote in a pre-game video message for the Spanish team.

Saadi al-Masri, 40 and captain of the amputee team in Gaza, watched the game with friends in a cafe. “I support Spain because we see it as a country that stands with the Palestinian cause and supports Palestinian rights,” he said.

Spain has been among Europe’s most vocal critics of Israel’s war on Gaza and state-backed violence in the occupied West Bank. It is pushing for stronger European Union action over human rights violations, including suspension of a broad free trade pact.

When Israel’s defence minister attacked Yamal for raising the Palestinian flag, accusing him of “inciting hatred”, the Spanish prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, was quick to defend the young player.

“Lamine has only expressed the solidarity with Palestine that is felt by millions of us in Spain. Another reason to be proud of him,” he said in a social media post.

Israeli support for Argentina was led by Netanyahu, who has cultivated close ties with far-right president Javier Milei, and posted a good luck message for the team ahead of the final.

The Palestinian delegation to the United Nations responded with an image of the Spanish team, under the headline “world champions”.

Even keen fans in Gaza have struggled to keep up with matches during the World Cup. Most of the 2 million Palestinians in the territory live in tent camps after Israeli attacks destroyed their homes, with little access to power or internet connections.

Arkan al-Walaida, 23, went to internet cafes to seek out match highlights each morning during the tournament, looking for short videos on TikTok or Fifa’s official YouTube and Instagram pages.

Key takeaways-Gazans gathered in makeshift cafes to watch Spain defeat Argentina 1-0 in the World Cup final, celebrating both the victory and Spain’s support for Palestine.

-Residents described the celebrations as an expression of gratitude toward a country widely seen as standing with Palestinians during Israel’s genocide in Gaza.

-The final capped months of symbolic gestures linking Spanish football and Palestinian solidarity, from Gaza’s amputee football team to supporters and players in Spain.

More than footballFor a few hours on Sunday night, the sounds of war gave way to football. Across the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza, small crowds gathered inside makeshift cafes, their attention fixed on flickering television screens broadcasting the FIFA World Cup final from MetLife Stadium in the United States.

When Spain’s Ferran Torres broke the deadlock in the 105th minute, beating Argentine goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez to secure a 1-0 victory after extra time, celebrations erupted.

For many in Gaza, however, the celebrations extended far beyond the football pitch.

People who gathered to watch the match said they supported Spain not only because of its football but because the country has increasingly come to symbolize solidarity with the Palestinian people during Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza.

Football offers a brief escapeThe World Cup final provided a rare moment of relief for Palestinians living under relentless bombardment, displacement and humanitarian hardship.

For several hours, football replaced the daily realities of survival, allowing families and friends to come together despite the difficult conditions.

Abdullah added that the gathering also carried a broader message of peace and solidarity with nations that have stood alongside the Palestinian cause, adding that Palestinians simply want to live in peace.

Spain’s victory secured the country’s second FIFA World Cup title, its first since winning the tournament in South Africa in 2010. The result also denied Argentina and Lionel Messi a second consecutive World Cup triumph following their victory in Qatar in 2022.

payload.title: Espanjan jalkapallon MM-voittoa juhlittiin Gazassa
payload.summary: Gazan asukkaat seurasivat Espanjan ja Argentiinan MM-finaalia tilapäiskahviloissa ja ulkoilmakatsomoissa. Espanjan 1–0-voitto merkitsi monille myös osoitusta palestiinalaisille annetusta tuesta.
payload.content:
Espanjan jalkapallomaajoukkueen maailmanmestaruutta juhlittiin Gazassa, jossa asukkaat kokoontuivat tilapäiskahviloihin ja ulkoilmakatsomoihin seuraamaan Argentiinaa vastaan pelattua loppuottelua. Espanjan 1–0-voitto sai alueella tavallista urheilutulosta laajemman merkityksen, sillä monet katsojat yhdistivät joukkueen Espanjan Palestiinaa tukevaan linjaan ja espanjalaisessa jalkapallossa nähtyihin solidaarisuuden eleisiin. Israelin Argentiinan joukkueelle osoittama tuki korosti osaltaan otteluun liitettyä poliittista asetelmaa.

## Pienet yleisöt seurasivat finaalia Nuseiratissa

Sunnuntai-iltana pieniä katsojaryhmiä kerääntyi muun muassa Gazan keskiosassa sijaitsevan Nuseiratin pakolaisleirin tilapäisiin kahviloihin. Ihmiset seurasivat MetLife Stadiumilla Yhdysvalloissa pelattua FIFA:n MM-finaalia televisioruuduilta, ja katsomoita syntyi myös ulos. Kokoontumiset järjestettiin vaikeissa oloissa ja Israelin iskujen vaarasta huolimatta. Lähteiden mukaan ruudut välkkyivät tilapäisissä katselupaikoissa, mutta pienet yleisöt pysyivät ottelun äärellä.

Ratkaisu syntyi jatkoajalla. Ferran Torres rikkoi maalittoman tilanteen 105. minuutilla ohittamalla Argentiinan maalivahdin Emiliano Martínezin. Maali jäi loppuottelun ainoaksi, joten Espanja varmisti maailmanmestaruuden 1–0-voitolla. Osuman jälkeen juhlat alkoivat katsomoissa ja Gazan kaduilla, joilla nähtiin Espanjan lippuja.

## Palestiinaa tukeneet eleet muistettiin

Monet paikalliset sanoivat kannattaneensa Espanjaa paitsi sen jalkapallon myös maan Palestiinaa tukevan linjan vuoksi. Voittoa pidettiin siksi kiitoksen ja solidaarisuuden ilmauksena, eikä finaali näyttäytynyt Gazassa pelkkänä Espanjan ja Argentiinan välisenä urheilukamppailuna. Espanjalaisen jalkapallon ja palestiinalaisten välille oli kertynyt symbolisia yhteyksiä jo turnausta edeltäneiden kuukausien aikana.

Erityistä huomiota sai Espanjan teinitähti Lamine Yamal, joka toi Palestiinan lipun Barcelonan Espanjan-liigan mestaruusjuhliin toukokuussa. Gazassa Espanjan lippuja heiluttaneet kannattajat osoittivat hänelle suosiotaan. Myös Gazan al-Irada-amputaatiojalkapallojoukkue lähetti ennen finaalia Espanjan joukkueelle videotervehdyksen: ”Se, joka nostaa Palestiinan lipun, ansaitsee nostaa myös maailmanmestaruuspokaalin”, joukkue kirjoitti.

## Jalkapallo tarjosi hetkellisen hengähdyksen

MM-finaali tarjosi Gazassa harvinaisen hengähdyshetken jatkuvien pommitusten, siirtymään joutumisen ja humanitaaristen vaikeuksien keskellä. Perheet ja ystävät pystyivät kokoontumaan yhteen ja keskittymään useiden tuntien ajan otteluun päivittäisen selviytymisen sijasta. Espanjan voiton juhlimisessa yhdistyivät siten urheilu ja palestiinalaisten kokema kansainvälinen solidaarisuus: he juhlivat sekä uutta maailmanmestaria että joukkueeseen ja sen ympärille liitettyjä Palestiinaa tukevia eleitä.
summary_bullets: Espanja voitti Argentiinan MM-finaalissa 1–0 jatkoajan jälkeen.
Ferran Torres teki ottelun ainoan maalin 105. minuutilla.
Gazan asukkaille Espanjan voitto symboloi myös tukea palestiinalaisille.
payload.journalist_note: Ottelutulos, maalintekijä sekä Gazan katsomoita ja juhlintaa koskevat tiedot ovat yhdenmukaiset paketin lähdekatkelmissa. Konfliktia koskevat poliittiset tulkinnat on esitetty asukkaiden näkemyksinä.

MM-finaali tarjosi Gazassa harvinaisen hengähdyshetken jatkuvien pommitusten, siirtymään joutumisen ja humanitaaristen vaikeuksien keskellä. Perheet ja ystävät pystyivät kokoontumaan yhteen ja keskittymään useiden tuntien ajan otteluun päivittäisen selviytymisen sijasta. Espanjan voiton juhlimisessa yhdistyivät siten urheilu ja palestiinalaisten kokema kansainvälinen solidaarisuus: he juhlivat sekä uutta maailmanmestaria että joukkueeseen ja sen ympärille liitettyjä Palestiinaa tukevia eleitä.

People gather at cafes and outdoor screenings to support team after Spain’s backing for Palestinian rights The Spanish football team’s World Cup win has been celebrated in the streets of Gaza, where Spain’s support for Palestinian rights and Israel’s backing for the Argentinian team turned the competition into more than a football showdown. Gathered at cafes and outdoor screenings, Palestinians defied the risk of Israeli attacks to cheer on a team they had taken to their hearts. Many waving Spanish flags paid tribute to teenage star Lamine Yamal, who brought a Palestinian flag to celebrations for Barcelona’s La Liga win in May. “Whoever raises the Palestinian flag deserves to raise the World Cup,” the Gaza al-Irada amputee football team wrote in a pre-game video message for the Spanish team.

Key takeaways-Gazans gathered in makeshift cafes to watch Spain defeat Argentina 1-0 in the World Cup final, celebrating both the victory and Spain’s support for Palestine. -Residents described the celebrations as an expression of gratitude toward a country widely seen as standing with Palestinians during Israel’s genocide in Gaza. -The final capped months of symbolic gestures linking Spanish football and Palestinian solidarity, from Gaza’s amputee football team to supporters and players in Spain. More than footballFor a few hours on Sunday night, the sounds of war gave way to football. Across the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza, small crowds gathered inside makeshift cafes, their attention fixed on flickering television screens broadcasting the FIFA World Cup final from MetLife Stadium in the United States.

When Spain’s Ferran Torres broke the deadlock in the 105th minute, beating Argentine goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez to secure a 1-0 victory after extra time, celebrations erupted. For many in Gaza, however, the celebrations extended far beyond the football pitch. People who gathered to watch the match said they supported Spain not only because of its football but because the country has increasingly come to symbolize solidarity with the Palestinian people during Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza. Football offers a brief escapeThe World Cup final provided a rare moment of relief for Palestinians living under relentless bombardment, displacement and humanitarian hardship. For several hours, football replaced the daily realities of survival, allowing families and friends to come together despite the difficult conditions.
